projects.name: PesaCore, a .NET 10 core banking platform
projects.description: Core banking platform on ASP.NET Core 10 with a Blazor front end: CQRS with idempotent transfers, PostgreSQL and Redis, OpenTelemetry, a hardened nginx edge, deployed on GCP Cloud Run.
projects.longDescription: A deployed, full-stack core-banking platform that began as a modern-.NET fluency signal and grew into a live cloud-native app. A Blazor WebAssembly SPA is fronted by an ASP.NET Core BFF (YARP reverse-proxy) that keeps the API URL and secrets server-side; because GCP Cloud Run scales to zero, durable state lives in Neon Postgres and shared/ephemeral state (distributed idempotency + cache-aside) in Upstash Redis — both serverless and swappable behind EF Core / IDistributedCache, so the vendor is a deployment choice, not a code dependency. CQRS via MediatR with a pipeline behavior enforcing an X-Idempotency-Key on every mutation (no double-debits across instances), FluentValidation at the request boundary, RFC 7807 problem responses, Polly resilience, OpenTelemetry (→ Collector → Prometheus → Grafana) and Serilog with correlation IDs, and a ReDoc/OpenAPI reference at /docs. One container, three front doors: Kestrel in a Linux container (Cloud Run), IIS + ANCM on-prem Windows (web.config, IISProfile.pubxml), or Azure — the same binary — bridging the .NET 4.5 / Windows Server era at Veracode to the current .NET LTS ecosystem. Secrets live only in GCP Secret Manager and are read at runtime; 67 tests (xUnit + WebApplicationFactory) gate CI; Husky.Net enforces pre-commit/pre-push. Operability and security are demonstrated end-to-end locally (make + docker): a hardened nginx edge acting as reverse-proxy / API gateway (TLS 1.2/1.3, HSTS, Content-Security-Policy and security headers, rate-limiting, gzip, and an upstream load-balancer across replicas); full observability (OpenTelemetry → Collector → Jaeger for distributed traces/APM, Prometheus + Grafana dashboards); and a local Kubernetes cluster (k3d/Kind + ingress-nginx + Horizontal Pod Autoscaler). Cloud infrastructure is captured as Terraform for GCP — authored and cost-gated so spend stays ~$0 (scale-to-zero; the managed load balancer + Web Application Firewall are behind a default-off flag).

projects.name: SwarmBench, multi-agent LLM study
projects.description: Empirical study of single-agent versus multi-agent LLM performance on software tasks, written as a Harbor benchmark across codebases up to 303K lines. No multi-agent advantage found for tool-using agents.
projects.longDescription: Designed and executed a seven-attempt empirical investigation of when multi-agent LLM decomposition beats single-agent execution. Tested three pre-registered hypotheses (codebase size, bug count, per-item research load) against Kimi K2.5 via Fireworks AI through the Harbor evaluation harness, spanning Python OSS bug-fix tasks (Click, Werkzeug, Apache Airflow at 303K LOC) and per-item structured CVE extraction (16 GitHub Security Advisories). Two hypotheses falsified outright; the third produced a 0.05 gap before the unified-authority pivot recovered the wedge mechanism. Headline finding: multi-agent decomposition cures context overflow on independent items, not capability ceilings or authority-disambiguation noise. Submitted attempt 7 under the assessment's oracle-only validation regime with reward = 1.0 confirmed via Harbor; produced a 5,129-word IMRAD-format preprint with 16 references for LinkedIn longform distribution.

projects.name: AgentPlane, AI project planning
projects.description: Project management tool where a three-agent LangGraph pipeline breaks an epic into estimated sub-tasks with a replayable audit log. FastAPI and Next.js with cost-bounded LLM calls.
projects.longDescription: Three-service monorepo combining a Plane-style issue tracker (FastAPI + CockroachDB) with a LangGraph supervisor pipeline and a Next.js 14 frontend. Three agents run in sequence: DecomposerAgent proposes 3–7 sub-issues using Anthropic forced tool-use, EstimatorAgent assigns Fibonacci story points with Fibonacci clamping, AssignerAgent recommends owners from the skills-tagged member roster and guards against hallucinated IDs. Results stream to the UI per-worker via SSE using LangGraph’s astream_events; every run is logged to MongoDB Atlas for replay and history diffing. Redis (Upstash, serverless free tier) enforces a 10 req/min/workspace sliding-window rate limit to cap Anthropic API spend. CockroachDB holds the workspace → project → issue hierarchy with self-referential parent_id for epics; LangGraph AsyncPostgresSaver checkpoints each worker so partial failures resume rather than restart. Deployed: Next.js 14 frontend on Vercel, FastAPI services on Fly.io free tier, CockroachDB Serverless (5 GB free), MongoDB Atlas M0 (512 MB free), Upstash Redis (10k req/day free).
